standard_prerequisites.name: The circle code
standard_prerequisites.statement: The code family assigns the integers to the base point, and its transport along the generating loop is what the lemma computes.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the family being transported in.

standard_prerequisites.name: Composition rule for transport
standard_prerequisites.statement: Transport along a path equals transport along the image of the path under the family, followed by transport in the family of types.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the first rewrite of the computation.

standard_prerequisites.name: Computation of the action on the loop and of univalence
standard_prerequisites.statement: The action of the code family on the generating loop is the successor equivalence on the integers, and transport along its image under univalence is the induced map on the integers.
standard_prerequisites.use: They are the last two rewrites that produce the arithmetic statement.

core_obligations: Compute the first equation in three steps: rewrite transport as transport along the action of the family and then in the family of types, identify the action on the generating loop with the successor equivalence, and evaluate the induced transport as addition of one (source lines 452-456).

Conclude the second equation from the first by observing that transport along a path and along its inverse are mutually inverse, so transport along the inverse loop must be the predecessor (source lines 457-459).

proof_roadmap.step: Three-step computation of the transport along the loop.
The inverse loop follows by the inverse relationship of transport.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author labelled lemma at source lines 447-450 (book Lemma 8.1.2): transporting an integer in the circle code along the generating loop yields its successor, and along the inverse loop its predecessor. The statement is arithmetic about a transport, and the proof (source lines 451-460) has to carry it out through three rewrites: the composition rule for transport, the computation of the action of the code family on the loop as the successor equivalence, and the computation of transport along the univalent image of that equivalence; only then does the arithmetic appear. The second equation is then obtained by the general fact that transports along a path and its inverse are mutually inverse, which is exactly why the second half costs no computation. Which rewrite supplies which factor is the whole content and the statement shows none of it.
